mil5.1.4:0.4: 4. Question On the Shaking of the Earth
mil5.1.4:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
mil5.1.4:1.2: ‘Bhikkhus, there are these eight causes and eight conditions for the appearance of a great earthquake.’
mil5.1.4:1.3: This was a complete statement, a statement without exception, a statement without alternative—there is no other ninth cause for the appearance of a great earthquake.
mil5.1.4:1.4: If, Venerable Nāgasena, there were another ninth cause for the appearance of a great earthquake, the Blessed One would have stated that cause too.
mil5.1.4:1.5: Since, Venerable Nāgasena, there is no other ninth cause for the appearance of a great earthquake, therefore it was not declared by the Blessed One. But this ninth cause for the appearance of a great earthquake is seen: when King Vessantara was giving the great offering, the great earth shook seven times.
mil5.1.4:1.6: If, Venerable Nāgasena, there are only eight causes and eight conditions for the appearance of a great earthquake, then the statement that when King Vessantara was giving the great offering the great earth shook seven times is false.
mil5.1.4:1.7: If when King Vessantara was giving the great offering the great earth shook seven times, then the statement that there are only eight causes and eight conditions for the appearance of a great earthquake is also false.
mil5.1.4:1.8: This is a dilemma with two horns, subtle, difficult to unravel, obscuring and profound. It has come to you; it cannot be resolved by another of inferior wisdom except by one as wise as you.”
mil5.1.4:2.1: And this too was said, your majesty, by the Blessed One:
mil5.1.4:2.2: ‘Bhikkhus, there are these eight causes and eight conditions for the appearance of a great earthquake.’
mil5.1.4:2.3: As for when the great earth shook seven times when King Vessantara was giving the great offering, that was untimely, occurring only once, separate from the eight causes; therefore it is not counted among the eight causes.
mil5.1.4:3.1: Just as, your majesty, in the world only three storm-clouds are counted: those of the rainy season, those of the winter, and those of the spring.
mil5.1.4:3.2: If apart from these another storm-cloud brings rain, that cloud is not counted among the recognized clouds; it is simply called an ‘unseasonable storm-cloud.’
mil5.1.4:3.3: Even so, your majesty, when the great earth shook seven times when King Vessantara was giving the great offering, that was untimely, occurring only once, separate from the eight causes; it is not counted among the eight causes.
mil5.1.4:4.1: Or again, your majesty, five hundred rivers flow from the Himalaya mountains, but of those five hundred rivers, only ten rivers are counted in the enumeration of rivers.
mil5.1.4:4.3: the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, Mahī, Sindhu, Sarassatī, Vetravatī, Vitaṁsa, and Candabhāga—the remaining rivers are not counted in the enumeration of rivers.
mil5.1.4:4.5: Those rivers do not have permanent water.
mil5.1.4:4.6: Even so, your majesty, when the great earth shook seven times when King Vessantara was giving the great offering, that was untimely, occurring only once, separate from the eight causes; it is not counted among the eight causes.
mil5.1.4:5.1: Or again, your majesty, a king may have one hundred, two hundred, or three hundred ministers, but only six persons are counted in the enumeration of ministers.
mil5.1.4:5.3: the commander-in-chief, the chief priest, the magistrate, the treasurer, the parasol bearer, and the sword bearer.
mil5.1.4:5.4: Only these are counted in the enumeration of ministers.
mil5.1.4:5.6: Because they are connected with the royal qualities; the rest are not counted, though they are all simply called ‘ministers.’
mil5.1.4:5.7: Even so, your majesty, when the great earth shook seven times when King Vessantara was giving the great offering, that was untimely, occurring only once, separate from the eight causes; it is not counted among the eight causes.
mil5.1.4:6.1: Have you heard, your majesty, at present in the Conqueror’s dispensation, of those who have performed meritorious service, whose kamma brings happiness in this very life, and whose fame has risen among gods and humans?”
mil5.1.4:6.2: “Yes, venerable sir, I have heard at present in the Conqueror’s dispensation of those who have performed meritorious service, whose kamma brings happiness in this very life, and whose fame has risen among gods and humans—seven persons.”
mil5.1.4:6.4: “Venerable sir, Sumana the garland-maker, Ekasātaka the brahmin, Puṇṇa the servant, Queen Mallikā, Queen Gopālamātā, the lay woman Suppiyā, and the slave woman Puṇṇā—these seven beings experience happiness in this very life, and their fame has risen among gods and humans.”
mil5.1.4:7.1: “And have you also heard of others in the past who went to the realm of the thirty-three gods bearing their human body?”
mil5.1.4:7.2: “Yes, venerable sir, I have heard of them.”
mil5.1.4:7.4: “Guttila the gandhabba, King Sādhīna, King Nimi, and King Mandhātā—these four persons are heard of as having gone to the realm of the thirty-three gods bearing their human body.”
mil5.1.4:7.5: “Even deeds done long ago are heard of as well done or badly done.
mil5.1.4:7.6: But have you heard before, your majesty, in the past period or in the present period, that when an offering was being given by such-and-such a person named so-and-so, the great earth shook once or twice or three times?”
mil5.1.4:7.8: “Although, your majesty, I have tradition, spiritual realization, learning, hearing, the power of training, careful listening, inquiry, and attendance on teachers—I too have never heard before that ‘when an offering was being given by such-and-such a person, the great earth shook once or twice or three times,’ except for the supreme gift of King Vessantara, the bull among kings.
mil5.1.4:7.9: And although, your majesty—between the two Buddhas, the Blessed One Kassapa and the Blessed One the Sakyan sage—hundreds of thousands of years beyond counting have passed, yet even there I have no report that ‘when an offering was being given by such-and-such a person, the great earth shook once or twice or three times.’
mil5.1.4:7.10: Not, your majesty, by that much effort, by that much exertion does the great earth shake. But laden with the weight of virtue, your majesty, laden with the weight of all praiseworthy qualities of action, unable to bear it, the great earth moves, quakes, and trembles.
mil5.1.4:8.1: Just as, your majesty, when a cart is laden with an excessive load, its hub and rim split and the axle breaks;
mil5.1.4:8.2: even so, your majesty, the great earth, laden with the weight of all praiseworthy qualities of action, unable to bear it, moves, quakes, and trembles.
mil5.1.4:9.1: Or again, your majesty, just as the sky, covered by the force of wind and water, laden with the weight of abundant water, struck by excessive wind, roars, resounds, and thunders;
mil5.1.4:9.2: even so, your majesty, the great earth, laden with the abundant and overwhelming weight of the power of King Vessantara’s giving, unable to bear it, moves, quakes, and trembles.
mil5.1.4:9.3: For, your majesty, King Vessantara’s mind did not proceed under the influence of lust, or under the influence of anger, nor under the influence of delusion, nor under the influence of conceit, nor under the influence of wrong view, nor under the influence of defilements, nor under the influence of unwholesome thoughts, nor under the influence of discontent, but rather it proceeded abundantly under the influence of giving.
